text: PREFACE This book is the direct sequel to Power.1 It has cost me much hard work and may, I fear, cost the reader no less.
text_raw:
PREFACE 
This book is the direct sequel to Power.1 It has cost me much hard 
work and may, I fear, cost the reader no less.

text: Anyone wishing to follow me will find himself engaged in a difficult piece of exploration, and I know well that I am not a good guide; but I feel strongly that this exploration is necessary and should be attempted by whoever would exercise the duties of a citizen with full awareness of what he is about.
text_raw:
Anyone wishing to 
follow me will find himself engaged in a difficult piece of exploration, 
and I know well that I am not a good guide; but I feel strongly that 
this exploration is necessary and should be attempted by whoever 
would exercise the duties of a citizen with full awareness of what he 
is about.

text: In a word, though what I say may be of small importance, the subject itself is of vast importance.
text_raw:
In a word, though what I say may be of small importance, 
the subject itself is of vast importance.

text: These meditations of mine, which have been taken up at intervals during the last nine years, have reverted progressively to the very heart of the problem of politics.
text_raw:
These meditations of mine, which have been taken up at intervals 
during the last nine years, have reverted progressively to the very 
heart of the problem of politics.

text: Each of us, even if he gives no thought to it, has a political activity and exercises an authority; we should achieve awareness of this role and of the obligations which it entails and should strive to play it better.
text_raw:
Each of us, even if he gives no 
thought to it, has a political activity and exercises an authority; we 
should achieve awareness of this role and of the obligations which 
it entails and should strive to play it better.

text: Politics as an everyday activity at once more widespread and more necessary than is commonly thought, authority as present in some degree in every man, the good to which this activity and this force, observable everywhere, should be directedâ€”these themes are inseparable from the inquiry undertaken in this book.
text_raw:
Politics as an everyday

commonly thought, authority as present in some degree in every 
man, the good to which this activity and this force, observable 
everywhere, should be directedâ€”these themes are inseparable from 
the inquiry undertaken in this book.

text: The first object of this inquiry was at once too limited as to its subject-matter and too ambitious in its aim.
text_raw:

text: It flowed directly from the preoccupation which gave birth to Power..

text: PREFACE causes (circumstances and ideas) have both disturbed and extended the public authority; they have shaped its course towards taking on ever wider and more numerous tasks, lacking all certain outline.
text_raw:
PREFACE 
causes (circumstances and ideas) have both disturbed and extended 
the public authority; they have shaped its course towards taking on 
ever wider and more numerous tasks, lacking all certain outline.

text: So it has come about that any fixed notion of its purpose, any sure preconception of its conduct, by which to judge whether it is doing too much or too little, has been lost.
text_raw:
So 
it has come about that any fixed notion of its purpose, any sure 
preconception of its conduct, by which to judge whether it is doing 
too much or too little, has been lost.

text: And political theorists, who for so long devoted themselves to the question of what was right for the public authority to do, are now concerned only to consider what is the right manner of its formation.
text_raw:
And political theorists, who 
for so long devoted themselves to the question of what was right 
for the public authority to do, are now concerned only to consider 
what is the right manner of its formation.

text: In the result, the only judgments now formed are on whether public authorities have a good title to act, not on whether they act well.
text_raw:
In the result, the only 
judgments now formed are on whether public authorities have a 
good title to act, not on whether they act well.

text: Originally, my objects were to tell in this book how the idea of the legitimate origin of Power has suppressed and driven out its natural fellow, that of the legitimate use of Power, and to drive home the loss thereby inflicted.
text_raw:
Originally, my objects were to tell in this book how the idea of 
the legitimate origin of Power has suppressed and driven out its 
natural fellow, that of the legitimate use of Power, and to drive home 
the loss thereby inflicted.

text: But what was the good of noting and emphasising this loss if no attempt was made to repair it?
text_raw:
But what was the good of noting and 
emphasising this loss if no attempt was made to repair it?

text: So it was that my original purpose drew me on to a search for the criteria applicable in our own day to the conduct of public authorities.
text_raw:
So it was 
that my original purpose drew me on to a search for the criteria 
applicable in our own day to the conduct of public authorities.

text: But the difficulty of such an undertaking is boundless.
text_raw:
But 
the difficulty of such an undertaking is boundless.

text: The thinkers of old could without difficulty picture clearly the ideal role of the public authority, for they thought, wrongly, that their society was static and unchanging, and that it was only a case of keeping in being a given state of things.
text_raw:
The thinkers of 
old could without difficulty picture clearly the ideal role of the 
public authority, for they thought, wrongly, that their society was 
static and unchanging, and that it was only a case of keeping in being 
a given state of things.

text: No less fortunate were those who held the opposite conception, that there existed an ideal order which had to be installed by revolutionary means and then would run on of itself: ardent destroyers of what they found, they were already conserving in anticipation a future Utopia.
text_raw:
No less fortunate were those who held the 
opposite conception, that there existed an ideal order which had to 
be installed by revolutionary means and then would run on of itself: 
ardent destroyers of what they found, they were already conserving 
in anticipation a future Utopia.
